name: ntopng
what_it_is: ntopng is a web-based network traffic monitoring application (GPLv3) that performs deep packet inspection via nDPI, real-time flow analysis, and alerting. It is the modernized successor to the original ntop project, supporting NetFlow, IPFIX, sFlow, SNMP, and eBPF-based packet capture.
components: Redis (required in-process state store for flows and alerts)
C++ core engine for packet/flow processing
Lua scripting layer for checks, alerts, and dashboards
protocols: nDPI / Deep Packet Inspection (application-layer protocol detection)
measurement: Real-time per-flow traffic statistics (bytes, packets, duration)
Top talkers and application-layer protocol breakdown
Historical flow data with configurable retention
Alert generation on threshold breaches, anomalies, and security events
Host behavioral analysis and reputation scoring
configuration: Network interface or probe input selection at startup (-i flag)
Community vs Enterprise edition feature gates (license key)
Lua-based behavioral checks and alert thresholds (editable scripts)
Data retention period for flow records
modes: Packet capture mode (live interface via libpcap/PF_RING/eBPF)
Flow collector mode (receives NetFlow/IPFIX/sFlow from external probes)
Community edition (free, GPLv3, limited feature set)
constraints: Requires a running Redis instance — ntopng will not start without it
No built-in docker-compose file found in main/dev branches; deployment must be scripted manually or via third-party images
Enterprise features (e.g., extended retention, advanced analytics) are not available under the GPLv3 community build
High-throughput environments require PF_RING or eBPF; standard libpcap becomes a bottleneck at multi-Gbps rates
notable_absences: No official docker-compose.yml found in the repository (checked main and dev branches)
No built-in fault or traffic replay injection mechanism
No native Kubernetes manifests in the repository
SNMP polling depth (MIB support) not documented in README
